text: Executes automated software regression tests using Python scripting, conducts human-in-the-loop quality assurance on generative AI outputs, evaluates prompt robustness against hallucination, and verifies algorithmic fairness.
Audits LLM responses and RAG citations for factual accuracy, designs structured prompt evaluation rubrics, logs human-in-the-loop validation metrics in SQL, and escalates bias or PDPA privacy leaks.

Monitors industrial energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions using Python data pipelines, SQL telemetry databases, and interactive BI dashboards to support Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR).

Maps factory floor production workflows and standard operating procedures under Malaysia Industry4WRD. Automates defect reporting pipelines via Python scripting, SQL analytics, and KPI visualization dashboards.

Oversees statutory compliance with Malaysia's amended Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), maps cross-border data flows, establishes redaction guardrails for generative AI tools, and trains staff on ethical data handling.

Leads enterprise-wide AI competency assessment, designs structured learning pathways for displaced clerical staff, tracks cohort reskilling KPIs via data visualization, and manages human-centred organizational change.

Extracts and reconciles financial transaction records using SQL queries, builds executive KPI dashboards and data visualizations, maps reporting processes, and presents analytical insights to leadership stakeholders.
Reads fixed telephone response scripts for routine status inquiries, logs basic ticket numbers manually, and transfers complex customer issues to senior supervisors.
Matches paper purchase orders against printed delivery notes, stamps physical payment vouchers, and archives paper ledger binders in storage rooms.

Key operational indicators include reskilling, upskilling, workforce training, vocational, education, competency, lifelong learning.

Occupation: software developer. Software developers implement or program all kinds of software systems based on specifications and designs by using programming languages, tools, and platforms. Core tasks and competencies: debug software; develop automated migration methods; technical drawings; analyse software specifications; identify customer requirements; use software libraries; utilise computer-aided software engineering tools; project management; engineering processes; engineering principles. Supplementary skills: Java (computer programming); PHP; World Wide Web Consortium standards; collect customer feedback on applications; CoffeeScript.

Occupation: embedded system designer. Embedded system designers translate and design requirements and the high-level plan or architecture of an embedded control system according to technical software specifications. Core tasks and competencies: real-time computing; task algorithmisation; signal processing; provide ICT consulting advice; create flowchart diagram; systems development life-cycle; define technical requirements; embedded systems; interpret electronic design specifications; analyse software specifications. Supplementary skills: ABAP; Prolog (computer programming); ICT network simulation; utilise computer-aided software engineering tools; SAS language.

Occupation: statistician. Statisticians collect, tabulate, and, most importantly, analyse quantitative information coming from a varied array of fields. They interpret and analyse statistical studies on fields such as health, demographics, finance, business, etc. and advise based on patterns and drawn analysis. Core tasks and competencies: identify statistical patterns; statistical analysis system software; apply scientific methods; apply statistical analysis techniques; process data; think analytically; data quality assessment; statistics; perform data analysis; mathematics. Supplementary skills: design questionnaires; provide lesson materials; advise on legislative acts; write scientific papers; conduct public surveys.

Occupation: ICT intelligent systems designer. ICT intelligent systems designers apply methods of artificial intelligence in engineering, robotics and computer science to design programs which simulate intelligence including thinking models, cognitive and knowledge-based systems, problem solving, and decision making. They also integrate structured knowledge into computer systems (ontologies, knowledge bases) in order to solve complex problems normally requiring a high level of human expertise or artificial intelligence methods. Core tasks and competencies: design database scheme; task algorithmisation; apply ICT systems theory; web programming; resource description framework query language; ICT security legislation; information structure; develop creative ideas; manage database; analyse business requirements. Supplementary skills: ASP.NET; Scala; Pascal (computer programming); build business relationships; Groovy.

Occupation: flight test engineer. Flight test engineers work with other systems engineers to plan the tests in detail and to make sure that the recording systems are installed for the required data parameters. They analyse the data collected during test flights and produce reports for individual test phases and for the final flight test. They are also responsible for the safety of the test operations. Core tasks and competencies: approve engineering design; operate radio navigation instruments; common aviation safety regulations; technical drawings; aircraft flight control systems; oversee aircraft sensors and recording systems; perform scientific research; plan test flights; industrial engineering; use technical drawing software. Supplementary skills: perform flight manoeuvres; aerospace engineering; electronics; instrumentation engineering; visual flight rules.

Occupation: maintenance and repair engineer. Maintenance and repair engineers focus on the optimization of equipment, procedures, machineries and infrastructure. They ensure their maximum availability at minimum costs. Core tasks and competencies: create solutions to problems; conduct quality control analysis; troubleshoot; advise on efficiency improvements; maintenance and repair; perform machine maintenance; conduct routine machinery checks; inspect machinery; write technical reports; maintain equipment. Supplementary skills: read standard blueprints; maintain nuclear reactors; nuclear energy; apply technical communication skills; total quality control.

Occupation: picture archiving and communication systems administrator. Picture archiving and communication systems administrators manage picture archiving and communication systems (PACS). They store images taken by various types of medical equipment, such as X-rays, in order to enable easy access to these images for medical. PACS administrators ensure the day-to-day management and maintenance of the system." Core tasks and competencies: medical terminology; attend to ICT systems quality; maintain ICT system; medical informatics; interact with healthcare users; administer ICT system; data protection; use electronic health records management system; project management; empathise with the healthcare user. Supplementary skills: implement strategic planning; radiological photography; Cisco; supplier management; provide cost benefit analysis reports.

Occupation: database administrator. Database administrators test, implement and administer computer databases. They use their expertise in database management systems to plan, coordinate and implement security measures to safeguard computer databases. They also use scripts and configuration files to tailor a database to users' needs. Core tasks and competencies: create data models; perform ICT troubleshooting; database development tools; information structure; balance database resources; maintain database security; manage database; operate relational database management system; interpret technical texts; define database physical structure. Supplementary skills: support ICT system users; use automatic programming; use different communication channels; business intelligence; provide technical documentation.

Occupation: product quality inspector. Product quality inspectors check products in order to assess their compliance in reference to a standard or reference guideline. They observe, measure, test, and form questions in order to fill in forms and present levels of compliance with comments after the inspection process. Product quality inspectors are employed or work externally for companies. Core tasks and competencies: identify process improvements; quality assurance procedures; perform quality audits; monitor manufacturing quality standards; manage corrective actions; identify preventive actions; negotiate with stakeholders; create solutions to problems; report defective manufacturing materials; support implementation of quality management systems. Supplementary skills: issue licences; recommend product improvements; operate precision measuring equipment; collect samples for analysis; train staff in quality procedures.

Occupation: leather goods quality control laboratory technician. Leather goods quality control laboratory technicians perform laboratory control tests according to the national and international standards. During laboratory control tests they prepare samples, address test procedures, analysis and interpretation of the results and comparison with guidelines and standards and prepare reports. They make the linkage with outsourced laboratories for the tests which cannot be performed inside the company. They propose corrective and preventive measures. Core tasks and competencies: manage footwear quality systems; leather goods components; use IT tools; apply footwear and leather goods quality control techniques; perform laboratory tests on footwear or leather goods; leather goods manufacturing processes; communicate commercial and technical issues in foreign languages; leather goods materials; reduce environmental impact of footwear manufacturing; leather goods quality. Supplementary skills: practice innovative thinking in the footwear and leather goods industries; use communication techniques.

Occupation: gambling, betting, and lottery quality assurance engineer. Gambling, betting and lottery quality assurance engineers design and plan methods to test the gambling, the lottery or betting games. They execute the tests. These games can be both for public or for private audience, and the tests are for both online and land-based gaming. Core tasks and competencies: report gaming incidents; probability theory; attend gaming tests; mathematics; legal standards in gambling; perform services in a flexible manner; solve problems in gambling through digital means; follow ethical code of conduct of gambling; develop work plans to solve problems. Supplementary skills: create game testing software; software components libraries; ICT software specifications; hardware components; SAS language.

Occupation: quality engineer. Quality engineers define quality standards for the creation of products or services. They check to make sure the products and services are in compliance with the quality standards and they coordinate quality improvements. Core tasks and competencies: identify improvement actions; report test findings; recommend product improvements; define quality standards; quality assurance methodologies; set quality assurance objectives; identify process improvements; perform risk analysis; record test data; quality standards. Supplementary skills: use measurement instruments; communication; oversee quality control; industrial engineering; maintain test equipment.

Occupation: quality services manager. Quality services managers manage the quality of services in business organisations. They ensure the quality of in-house company operations such as customer requirements and service quality standards. Quality services managers monitor the company's performance and implement changes where necessary. Core tasks and competencies: create solutions to problems; perform quality audits; database quality standards; business processes; quality standards; corporate social responsibility; business knowledge; analyse test data; train staff in quality procedures; improve business processes. Supplementary skills: perform project management; set quality assurance objectives; analyse business processes; provide technical documentation; use measurement instruments.

Occupation: occupational analyst. Occupational analysts collect and analyse occupational information within one field or company in order to make recommendations for reducing costs and general business improvements. They provide technical assistance to employers in dealing with problematic staff recruitment and development and with staff restructuring. Occupational analysts study and write job descriptions and prepare occupational classification systems. Core tasks and competencies: design job analysis tools; present reports; employment law; advise on personnel management; advise on efficiency improvements; company policies; job market offers; human resource management; write work-related reports; labour legislation. Supplementary skills: organise training; liaise with union officials; document interviews; identify necessary human resources; develop training programmes.

Occupation: digital printer. Digital printers work with machines that print directly to the medium, without an intervening plate. Digital printers usually use laser or inkjet technology to print individual pages without lengthy or labour intensive technical steps intervening between the finished digital product and the print. Core tasks and competencies: use colour printing programs; maintenance of printing machines; monitor automated machines; printing materials; follow production schedule; supply machine; set colour profiles; digital printing; perform test run; operate digital printers. Supplementary skills: printing media; keep records of work progress; inspect printing output; perform machine maintenance; record production data for quality control.

Occupation: environmental programme coordinator. Environmental programme coordinators develop programmes for the improvement of environmental sustainability and efficiency within a organisation or institution. They inspect sites in order to monitor an organisation's or institution's compliance with environmental legislation. They also ensure education for the public on environmental concerns. Core tasks and competencies: perform environmental investigations; implement environmental action plans; implement environmental protection measures; promote environmental awareness; assess environmental impact; environmental legislation; conduct environmental surveys; analyse environmental data; environmental policy; carry out environmental audits. Supplementary skills: ecology; radiation protection; carry out training in environmental matters; write inspection reports; liaise with local authorities.

Occupation: hazardous materials inspector. Hazardous materials inspectors inspect facilities which handle hazardous materials to ensure compliance to health and safety regulations, and hazardous materials handling legislation. They investigate violations, oversee tests of emergency and risk response plans, and consult on the improvement of the facilities' operations and procedures, as well as on hazardous materials regulations. They also advise plants on potential sources of danger to a community, and on better safety regulations. Core tasks and competencies: revise certifications for dangerous good transportation; hazardous materials transportation; pollution prevention; develop hazardous waste management strategies; waste management; ensure compliance with waste legislative regulations; inspect compliance with hazardous waste regulations; radioactive contamination; hazardous waste types; waste and scrap products. Supplementary skills: radiation protection; test safety strategies; wear appropriate protective gear; train staff on waste management; educate on hazardous waste.

Occupation: environmental mining engineer. Environmental mining engineers oversee the environmental performance of mining operations. They develop and implement environmental systems and strategies to minimise environmental impacts. Core tasks and competencies: develop environmental policy; communicate on the environmental impact of mining; use a computer; ensure compliance with safety legislation; use technical drawing software; adjust engineering designs; communicate on minerals issues; troubleshoot; perform scientific research; chemistry. Supplementary skills: present reports; negotiate with stakeholders; impact of meteorological phenomena on mining operations; develop mine rehabilitation plan; biology.

Occupation: radiation protection officer. Radiation protection officers are responsible for the protection from harmful effects caused by exposure to ionising radiation. They ensure compliance with legislation and regulations by enforcing safety measures. Furthermore they develop radiation protection plans in particular for nuclear plants and facilities. Core tasks and competencies: develop radiation protection strategies; nuclear legislation; ensure compliance with radiation protection regulations; monitor radiation levels; follow nuclear plant safety precautions; pollution prevention; ensure compliance with environmental legislation; environmental legislation; radiation physics in healthcare; nuclear physics. Supplementary skills: investigate pollution; pollution legislation; investigate contamination; inspect government policy compliance; monitor disposal of radioactive substances.

Occupation: data quality specialist. Data quality specialists review organisation's data for accuracy, recommend enhancements to record systems and data acquisition processes and assess referential and historical integrity of data. They also develop documents and maintain data quality goals and standards and oversee an organisation's data privacy policy and monitor compliance of data flows against data quality standards. Core tasks and competencies: design database scheme; implement data quality processes; information structure; resource description framework query language; establish data processes; manage database; process data; manage standards for data exchange; manage data; perform data cleansing. Supplementary skills: perform project management; LINQ; N1QL; manage schedule of tasks; execute analytical mathematical calculations.

Occupation: licensing officer. Licensing officers process licence applications and provide advice on licensing legislation. They also perform investigative duties to ensure the applicant is eligible for the requested licence, ensure licence fees are paid in a timely manner, and ensure compliance with legislation. Core tasks and competencies: assess breaches of licence agreements; prepare licence agreements; correspond with licence applicants; assess licence applications; advise on licencing procedures; licences regulation; grant concessions; public service concession; manage licensing fees; monitor compliance with licensing agreements. Supplementary skills: conduct research interview; office software; use microsoft office; keep task records; ensure proper document management.

Occupation: call centre quality auditor. Call centre quality auditors listen to calls from the call centre operators, recorded or live, in order to assess compliance with protocols and quality parameters. They grade the employees and provide feedback on the issues that require improvement. They interpret and spread quality parameters received by the management. Core tasks and competencies: maintain high quality of calls; guarantee customer satisfaction; assess employees' capability levels; quality standards; measure customer feedback; report call errors; provide objective assessments of calls; provide feedback on job performance; measure call quality; information confidentiality. Supplementary skills: advise on organisation climate; advise on efficiency improvements; call-centre technologies; business management principles; train employees.

Occupation: financial auditor. Financial auditors collect and examine financial data for clients, organisations and companies. They ensure the financial data is properly maintained and free of material misstatements due to error or fraud, that it adds up, and functions legally and effectively. They review lending and credit policies or numbers in databases and documents, evaluate, consult and assist the source of the transaction if necessary. They use their review of the client's financial governance as assurance to give testimony to the shareholders, stakeholders and board of directors of the organisation or company that all is up to par. Core tasks and competencies: interpret financial statements; accounting department processes; inspect tax returns; conduct financial audits; obtain financial information; accounting; analyse financial risk; pose questions referring to documents; corporate law; check accounting records. Supplementary skills: idenfify if a company is a going concern; advise on tax planning; fraud detection; joint ventures; financial statements.

Occupation: sales support assistant. Sales support assistants perform a variety of general sales support tasks, such as supporting the development of sales plans, managing clerical activities of sales efforts, verifying client invoices and other accounting documents or records, compiling data, and preparing reports for other company departments. Core tasks and competencies: perform clerical duties; handle mail; perform business research; sales activities; perform office routine activities; bookkeeping regulations. Supplementary skills: customer service; issue sales invoices; implement sales strategies; analyse customer service surveys; order supplies.

occupation_family: MASCO 41/42 (Clerical Support - High Automation Risk in MY)
text: Occupation: data entry clerk. Data entry clerks update, maintain and retrieve information held on computer systems. They prepare source data for computer entry by compiling and sorting information, process customer and account source documents by reviewing data for deficiencies and verify entered customer and account data. Core tasks and competencies: apply information security policies; maintain data entry requirements; apply statistical analysis techniques; query languages; process data; database; resource description framework query language; documentation types; perform data cleansing. Supplementary skills: LINQ; MDX; normalise data; OmniPage; SPARQL.

occupation_family: MASCO 41/42 (Clerical Support - High Automation Risk in MY)
text: Occupation: data entry supervisor. Data entry supervisors manage the day-to-day operations of data entry staff. They organise the workflow and tasks.  Core tasks and competencies: MDX; apply information security policies; LDAP; estimate duration of work; N1QL; motivate employees; supervise work; manage schedule of tasks; resource description framework query language; company policies. Supplementary skills: manage data collection systems; recruit employees; manage ICT data classification; discharge employees; establish data processes.

Occupation: medical administrative assistant. Medical administrative assistants work very closely with health professionals. They provide office support such as correspondence, fixing appointments and answering queries of patients. Core tasks and competencies: manage budgets; collect healthcare user's general data; manage personnel agenda; type on electronic devices; answer patients' questions; maintain healthcare user data confidentiality; apply organisational techniques; send medical samples; medical informatics; administrative tasks in a medical environment. Supplementary skills: process medical insurance claims; pathology; allocate bills; work in a multicultural environment in health care; organise travel arrangements for staff.

Occupation: train attendant. Train attendants work on trains to provide services to passengers such as welcoming passengers, answering their questions and serving meals. Core tasks and competencies: serve food in table service; greet guests; comply with food safety and hygiene; maintain customer service; handle financial transactions; health and safety measures in transportation. Supplementary skills: handle guest luggage; read stowage plans; handle customer complaints; assist passengers with timetable information; service rooms.

Occupation: ICT help desk agent. ICT help desk agents provide technical assistance to computer users, answer questions or solve computer problems for clients via telephone or electronically. They provide assistance concerning the use of computer hardware and software. Core tasks and competencies: use customer relationship management software; communicate with customers; characteristics of services; product comprehension; provide ICT support; keep task records; prioritise requests; keep up to date on product knowledge; support ICT system users; identify customer's needs. Supplementary skills: ICT help platforms; educate on data confidentiality; perform escalation procedure; handle helpdesk problems; ICT infrastructure.

Occupation: application engineer. Application engineers deal with the technical requirements, management, and design for the development of various engineering applications, such as systems, new product designs, or the improvements of processes. They are responsible for the implementation of a design or process improvement, they offer technical support for products, answer questions about the technical functionality and assist the sales team. Core tasks and competencies: perform scientific research; technical drawings; interpret technical requirements; use technical drawing software; engineering processes; engineering principles; define technical requirements; project management; manage engineering project. Supplementary skills: Vagrant; use translation memory software; identify suppliers; labour legislation; execute feasibility study.

Occupation: biochemical engineer. Biochemical engineers research on the field of life science striving for new discoveries. They convert those findings into chemical solutions that can improve the wellbeing of society such as vaccines, tissue repair, crops improvement and green technologies advances such as cleaner fuels from natural resources. Core tasks and competencies: test samples for pollutants; examine engineering principles; interpret 3D plans; advise on manufacturing problems; good manufacturing practices; advise on nitrate pollution; develop biochemical manufacturing training materials; use chromatography software; manage chemical testing procedures; gas chromatography. Supplementary skills: pharmaceutical drug development; develop biocatalytic processes; pharmaceutical chemistry; packaging processes; food materials.

Occupation: clinical psychologist. Clinical psychologists diagnose, rehabilitate, and support individuals affected by mental, emotional, and behavioural disorders and problems as well as mental changes and pathogenic conditions through use of cognitive tools and appropriate intervention. They use clinical psychological resources on the basis of psychological science, its findings, theories, methods, and techniques for the investigation, interpretation, and prediction of human experience and behaviour. Core tasks and competencies: empathise with the healthcare user; refer healthcare users; develop a collaborative therapeutic relationship; assess healthcare users' risk for harm; organise relapse prevention; use e-health and mobile health technologies; counsel clients; creation of clinical psychological opinions; accept own accountability; emergency psychology. Supplementary skills: employ foreign languages for health-related research; work with healthcare users' social network; ensure proper appointment administration; apply hypno-psychotherapy; apply caseload management.

Occupation: business manager. Business managers are responsible for setting the objectives of the business unit of a company, creating a plan for the operations, and facilitating the achievement of the objectives and implementation of the plan together with employees of the segment and stakeholders. They keep an overview of the business, understand detailed information of the business unit and support the department, and make decisions based on the information at hand. Core tasks and competencies: apply business acumen; corporate social responsibility; create a financial plan; liaise with managers; create a work atmosphere of continuous improvement; develop business plans; develop revenue generation strategies; develop company strategies; business law; assume responsibility for the management of a business. Supplementary skills: share good practices across subsidiaries; market entry planning; impart business plans to collaborators; oversee quality control; international trade.

Occupation: ICT product manager. ICT product managers analyse and define current and target status for ICT products, services or solutions. They estimate the cost effectiveness, points of risk, opportunities, strengths and weaknesses of products or services provided. ICT product managers create structured plans and establish time scales and milestones, ensuring optimisation of activities and resources. Core tasks and competencies: advertising techniques; product comprehension; cost management; ICT infrastructure; create project specifications; perform risk analysis; ICT system user requirements; manage contracts; manage budgets; ICT market. Supplementary skills: business process modelling; Waterfall development; service-oriented modelling; manage localisation; ICT process quality models.
